burning smell.note: Turn the system off and call a technician promptly — do not keep running it.

not heating or cooling.note: Check the thermostat, breaker, and filter first; if all fine, call a technician.

weak airflow.note: A clogged filter is the most common cause — replace it and recheck vents.

ice maker not working.note: Check the water supply line and the ice maker arm/switch before calling anyone.

not cooling.note: Check thermostat setting and vents first; if still warm, call service — compressor issues are not DIY.

strange noise.note: Rattling is often an unlevel unit or items vibrating on top; persistent buzzing needs a technician.

chirping.note: Usually a low battery — replace it; if chirping continues the unit may be expired.

false alarms.note: Dust the sensor and check placement away from kitchens/bathrooms; persistent false alarms mean replace.

no sound on test.note: Replace batteries first; if still silent, replace the whole unit immediately.

leaking from tank.note: A leaking tank generally means replacement, not repair. Shut off water and power.

no hot water.note: Check the breaker/thermostat first; gas or element failures need a technician.

rumbling or popping noise.note: Usually sediment buildup — flushing the tank often fixes it.

bad taste or odor.note: Replace the cartridge and sanitize the system; if it persists, check the source water.

leaking.note: Shut off the inlet valve and call service — leaks risk water damage.

slow water flow.note: Almost always an expired filter cartridge — replace it first.

note: HomeKeeper Appliance Catalog — static knowledge base and the hallucination guard. The model may extract brand/model from a photo, but maintenance intervals, warranty lengths, and triage guidance ALWAYS come from this table, never from the LLM.
